title: Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture
formal: Does every finite clutter with the packing property have the max-flow min-cut property? Equivalently, if every deletion/contraction minor satisfies unweighted integral packing–covering equality, must weighted integral packing–covering equality hold for every nonnegative integer weight vector?
definitions:
A clutter C on a finite ground set E is a family of subsets of E, no one properly containing another. In the original instance all members are nonempty; the empty family is allowed. A cover \(T\subseteq E\) meets every member, and \(	au (C)\) is the smallest cover size. A packing is a family of pairwise disjoint members, with maximum size \(
u (C)\). Deleting e removes e from the ground set and discards all members containing e. Contracting e removes it from the ground set and from every member, and retains only inclusion-minimal resulting members. A minor results from any sequence of these operations. The packing property means \(	au (C' )=
u (C' )\) for every minor \(C'\). For the empty family both values are zero; for a minor containing the empty set both are defined as +∞, with the empty member permitted arbitrarily many times in a packing. For \(w\in \mathbb{Z} _{\ge 0}^{E}\), let \(	au _{w}(C)=\min\){\(\sum_{e\in T}w_{e}:T\) covers C}. Let \(
u _{w}(C)\) be the maximum of \(\sum_{F\in C}y_{F}\) over nonnegative integers \(y_{F}\) satisfying \(\Sigma\)_{F∋e}\(y_{F}\le w_{e}\) for every \(e\in E\). Thus a weighted packing may use a member repeatedly, subject to capacities w. The max-flow min-cut property is \(	au _{w}(C)=
u _{w}(C)\) for every such w. The original nonempty-member assumption makes these weighted optima finite.
answer_criterion: Prove that the packing property implies \(\tau _{w}=\nu _{w}\) for every finite clutter and every nonnegative integer weight vector, or give a finite clutter and weight vector with the packing property and \(\tau _{w}>\nu _{w}\). A counterexample must verify equality for all minors, not merely for the original unweighted clutter. Finite searches, proofs for a proper subclass, or fractional optimality alone do not resolve the universal statement.

context_blocks.text: Packing and covering often give two descriptions of the same combinatorial optimum. In a clutter, the unweighted equality can fail. Requiring equality after every deletion and contraction removes many such obstructions. The Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture asks whether this local robustness already guarantees equality for every integer capacity vector.

For a concrete example, take E as the vertices of a bipartite graph and the clutter members as its edges. Covers are vertex covers and packings are matchings. This illustrates the familiar kind of min–max equality that the general conjecture seeks to characterize, without restricting its input to graph edge families.

If A is the member-by-element incidence matrix, the associated linear programs are \(\min  w^{T}x\) subject to \(Ax\ge 1\) and \(x\ge 0\), and \(\max  1^{T}y\) subject to \(A^{T}y\le w\) and \(y\ge 0\). Equality of the two integer optima forces their values to agree with the fractional optimum by weak and strong duality. This is the standard MFMC integrality requirement.

Schrijver’s Survey Question 68 calls the target the assertion that every packing hypergraph is Mengerian. The terminology differs, but its packing property includes all minors and its conclusion includes arbitrary nonnegative integer weights. Checking only the all-ones weight on the original instance would yield a much weaker, insufficient hypothesis.

Abdi and Schwarcz’s July 2026 manuscript calls the statement the replication conjecture and explicitly retains it as open. It reports verification for clutters on at most ten elements and for a specified bounded-degree family of cuboids. These are finite or restricted confirmations, not a proof for arbitrary ground-set size.

The same work gives a finite set of weight vectors sufficient to test the MFMC property of a fixed clutter, with an improved bound on their entries. This makes checking individual instances more effective. The number and size of possible clutters still grow without bound, so instance-wise testability does not prove the universal implication.

why: Identify whether all obstructions to weighted integral packing–covering duality are already visible as unweighted failures in minors, a central issue in integer programming and combinatorial optimization.

importance.reason: A central conjecture connecting minor obstructions, integral linear programming and packing–covering duality. Schrijver treats it as a major survey question, and a July 2026 primary paper develops both theoretical and computational methods around it.

progress.text: Schrijver lists the packing-to-Mengerian implication as Survey Question 68.
Abdi–Schwarcz v2 reports finite verification through ten ground-set elements and an improved finite-weight test, while leaving the universal conjecture open.

status_note: No general resolution was found through 11 September 2026. The checked July 2026 manuscript explicitly retains the conjecture. Its reported finite computations and subclass results are recorded as progress; their proof artifacts were not independently rechecked in this editorial review.
review_note: Formulation checked against Schrijver Question 68 and Abdi–Schwarcz v2. Minor operations, degenerate minors, integer weights and repeated packed members are explicit. No equivalent clutter/Mengerian/packing-property target was found in active or archived catalogue records.
